Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test checks:
  - The test adds a case that calls TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Other.class, This.class) and expects a mapping for both of This’s type variables:
    - This’s first type variable should map to String.
    - This’s second type variable should map to the (still unbound) type variable declared by Other (i.e., a partially-assigned class should still propagate its type variable up to the target type).

- Expected type relationship:
  - The scenario implied by the assertions is of the form:
    - class This<A, B> { ... }
    - class Other<T> extends This<String, T> { ... }
  - Therefore, getTypeArguments(Other.class, This.class) should return a map of size 2:
    - This<A> -> String
    - This<B> -> Other’s T (a TypeVariable)

- How the current implementation behaves:
  - The public entry TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Type, Class<?>) delegates to a private overload based on the runtime type of the first argument.
  - Because the first argument is a Class (Other.class), the flow goes into:
    - getTypeArguments(Class<?>, Class<?>, Map<TypeVariable<?>, Type>) at lines ~650+.
  - In that method:
    - It confirms assignability (Other is assignable to This) and prepares a new map.
    - Then it has an early-return guard:
      - if (cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0 || toClass.equals(cls)) { return typeVarAssigns; } (lines ~675–677)
    - This is incorrect. For Other.class, cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0 (because Other declares T), so it returns immediately with the current (empty) map, without walking up the hierarchy to This and without collecting type variable assignments.

- Why this causes the failure:
  - The early return in the Class<?> overload falsely treats “source class declares type parameters” as “target reached,” which prevents traversing to the target supertype (This) and computing its type argument bindings.
  - Consequently, the returned map is empty instead of having the two expected entries, making the test’s size() == 2 assertion fail.

- Evidence in the code:
  - TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Type, Class<?>): returns getTypeArguments(type, toClass, null).
  - TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Type, Class<?>, Map<...>): dispatches to the Class<?> overload for Class input.
  - TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Class<?>, Class<?>, Map<...>) (lines ~650–681):
    - The problematic condition is:
      - if (cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0 || toClass.equals(cls)) { return typeVarAssigns; }
    - This causes premature termination for partially-assigned source classes like Other<T>.
  - Contrast with the ParameterizedType overload (lines ~597–640):
    - It correctly maps type arguments to type variables and walks the hierarchy until the target class is reached.
    - However, it is bypassed here because the call site passes a Class, not a ParameterizedType.

- Conclusion (root cause):
  - The Class-based overload of getTypeArguments() terminates early whenever the source class declares type parameters, even if the target class has not been reached. This prevents propagating partially-bound type variables through the inheritance chain, which is exactly what the failing test (and bug report) require. Removing the “cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0” part of the early-return condition (so that it only returns when toClass.equals(cls)) will allow the method to walk up to This and compute the correct 2-entry mapping.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
